claim: Spinal pain affects individuals of all ages and is the most common musculoskeletal problem globally.
source: Spinal pain affects individuals of all ages and is the most common musculoskeletal problem globally.
evidence: This is a general statement about spinal pain prevalence that draws from established medical knowledge.

claim: Significantly increased numbers of senescent osteoclasts (SnOCs) are observed in mouse models of spinal hypersensitivity, like lumbar spine instability (LSI) or aging, compared to controls.
source: Here, we report that significantly increased numbers of senescent osteoclasts (SnOCs) are observed in mouse models of spinal hypersensitivity, like lumbar spine instability (LSI) or aging, compared to controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the study comparing SnOC numbers across different mouse models.

claim: The larger population of SnOCs is associated with induced sensory nerve innervation in the porous endplate.
source: The larger population of SnOCs is associated with induced sensory nerve innervation, as well as the growth of H-type vessels, in the porous endplate.
evidence: This association is demonstrated through experimental observations in the study.

claim: The larger population of SnOCs is associated with the growth of H-type vessels in the porous endplate.
source: The larger population of SnOCs is associated with induced sensory nerve innervation, as well as the growth of H-type vessels, in the porous endplate.
evidence: This association is demonstrated through experimental observations in the study.

claim: Deletion of senescent cells by administration of the senolytic drug Navitoclax (ABT263) results in significantly less spinal hypersensitivity.
source: We show that deletion of senescent cells by administration of the senolytic drug Navitoclax (ABT263) results in significantly less spinal hypersensitivity, spinal degeneration, porosity of the endplate, sensory nerve innervation, and H-type vessel growth in the endplate.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from behavioral tests after ABT263 treatment.

claim: Deletion of senescent cells by administration of ABT263 results in significantly less spinal degeneration.
source: We show that deletion of senescent cells by administration of the senolytic drug Navitoclax (ABT263) results in significantly less spinal hypersensitivity, spinal degeneration, porosity of the endplate, sensory nerve innervation, and H-type vessel growth in the endplate.
evidence: This is supported by histological and μCT data showing reduced degeneration markers.

claim: Deletion of senescent cells by administration of ABT263 results in significantly less porosity of the endplate.
source: We show that deletion of senescent cells by administration of the senolytic drug Navitoclax (ABT263) results in significantly less spinal hypersensitivity, spinal degeneration, porosity of the endplate, sensory nerve innervation, and H-type vessel growth in the endplate.
evidence: This is supported by μCT quantitative analysis of endplate porosity.

claim: Deletion of senescent cells by administration of ABT263 results in significantly less sensory nerve innervation.
source: We show that deletion of senescent cells by administration of the senolytic drug Navitoclax (ABT263) results in significantly less spinal hypersensitivity, spinal degeneration, porosity of the endplate, sensory nerve innervation, and H-type vessel growth in the endplate.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescent staining data showing reduced nerve markers.

claim: Deletion of senescent cells by administration of ABT263 results in significantly less H-type vessel growth in the endplate.
source: We show that deletion of senescent cells by administration of the senolytic drug Navitoclax (ABT263) results in significantly less spinal hypersensitivity, spinal degeneration, porosity of the endplate, sensory nerve innervation, and H-type vessel growth in the endplate.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescent staining data showing reduced vessel markers.

claim: There is significantly increased SnOC-mediated secretion of Netrin-1 compared to non-senescent OCs.
source: We also show that there is significantly increased SnOC-mediated secretion of Netrin-1 and NGF, two well-established sensory nerve growth factors, compared to non-senescent OCs.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR and ELISA data showing increased expression and concentration of Netrin-1.

claim: There is significantly increased SnOC-mediated secretion of NGF compared to non-senescent OCs.
source: We also show that there is significantly increased SnOC-mediated secretion of Netrin-1 and NGF, two well-established sensory nerve growth factors, compared to non-senescent OCs.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR and ELISA data showing increased expression and concentration of NGF.

claim: Netrin-1 is a well-established sensory nerve growth factor.
source: We also show that there is significantly increased SnOC-mediated secretion of Netrin-1 and NGF, two well-established sensory nerve growth factors, compared to non-senescent OCs.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about Netrin-1's role in nerve growth.

claim: NGF is a well-established sensory nerve growth factor.
source: We also show that there is significantly increased SnOC-mediated secretion of Netrin-1 and NGF, two well-established sensory nerve growth factors, compared to non-senescent OCs.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about NGF's role in nerve growth.

claim: Pharmacological elimination of SnOCs may be a potent therapy to treat spinal pain.
source: These findings suggest that pharmacological elimination of SnOCs may be a potent therapy to treat spinal pain.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings of the study.

claim: Cellular senescence is a stable and terminal state of growth arrest in which cells are unable to proliferate despite optimal growth conditions and mitogenic stimuli.
